programs.name: Brass Swell I
programs.description: A rounded body arrives first, then a brighter second rank blooms over roughly half a second. Pressure opens the held chord; the wheel adds restrained vibrato.

programs.name: Brass Swell II
programs.description: A 16' foundation supports an 8' brass crown. Their staggered filter rises give a broad low swell; pressure brings forward the upper rank.

programs.name: Pressure Swell Brass
programs.description: A quiet, dark chord waits under the fingers. Pressure supplies most of its level and brightness; releasing pressure brings it back to the soft bed.

programs.name: Resonant Swell Brass
programs.description: A focused resonant edge rises above a warmer body, then settles into a sustained brass chord. The two filter peaks arrive at different times.

programs.name: Noir Swell Brass
programs.description: A wide, slow brass bloom with a dark center and a luminous upper rank. Pressure adds brightness and gentle vibrato; the long release supports spacious chords.

programs.name: Sforzando Brass
programs.description: A bright, hard-struck accent relaxes into a quieter sustained section. One rank carries the initial bite while the other holds the body.

programs.name: Brass Stab
programs.description: A short, dry brass hit with a rounded low attack and a brighter upper bite. Both ranks decay away even while the key remains held; velocity controls the accent.

programs.name: Horn Section
programs.description: A mellow saw body and softer pulse edge form a compact horn section. Slightly staggered attacks avoid a hard synth click; pressure gives a modest brass bloom.

programs.name: Covered Horn
programs.description: Dark, rounded horn phrasing with a small sine foundation and a quiet covered edge. Pressure shapes level more strongly than brightness; use the middle and lower registers.

programs.name: Muted Trumpet
programs.description: A dry, narrow brass body with a focused nasal pulse edge, voiced as a muted-trumpet interpretation. Firm strikes sharpen the attack; pressure gives a small expressive vibrato.

programs.name: Trombone Glide
programs.description: A low 16' brass voice with a gentle upward lip scoop and portamento for slide-like phrases. A quieter edge rank follows the body without chorus.

programs.name: Fanfare Brass
programs.description: An assertive 8' section with a shorter 4' crown. The octave brightens the opening accent without dominating the held chord; firm strikes bring out the fanfare bite.

programs.name: Brass Ensemble 16
programs.description: A weighty 16' body under an 8' section, with restrained chorus for ensemble width. The upper rank enters a little later and stays lighter than the foundation.

programs.name: Low Brass
programs.description: Two 16' ranks combine a rounded saw foundation with a darker pulse edge. A slower low-body attack gives weight without the constant wobble of an ensemble effect.

programs.name: Velvet Brass
programs.description: A soft brass pad with a rounded sine-supported center and a delayed, dark pulse halo. Gentle pressure adds warmth and level; the chorus softens the edges.

programs.name: Bright Brass Poly
programs.description: A fast, bright brass comping patch. The body sustains while a more percussive upper edge relaxes after each chord; short releases keep rhythmic changes clear.

programs.name: Brass Pad Swell
programs.description: A chord pad whose rounded body rises over a second before a brighter rank completes the bloom. Hold notes to hear the full swell and overlapping release.

programs.name: Fifth Brass
programs.description: An 8' brass body with a quieter 5 1/3' rank at a harmonic fifth. The fifth has its own brighter filter and softer sustain, so the played root remains clear.

programs.name: Wah Brass
programs.description: A stable brass body acquires a rhythmic filter wah as pressure feeds the sine SUB into the VCF. The wheel adds a small independent vibrato.

programs.name: Synth Horns
programs.description: A firm saw body beneath a saw-and-pulse upper rank. Slow, shallow pulse-width movement supplies thickness without turning every note into a chorus wash.

programs.name: Brass Bite
programs.description: Soft strikes remain rounded; hard strikes raise a focused resonant bite and a stronger upper-rank accent. Pressure adds a smaller bloom after the attack.

programs.name: Distant Brass
programs.description: A softened brass ensemble with a dark center, slow entrances and a long, diffuse release. Deep chorus supplies distance; the upper edge stays deliberately subdued.

programs.name: Brass Crescendo
programs.description: The body takes 1.6 seconds to reach full amplitude while the upper rank blooms more slowly. Hold the chord through the rise, then use pressure to sustain the intensity.

programs.name: Cuivre Brass
programs.description: A rounded low-pressure brass body gains an assertive, resonant upper edge as pressure rises. The body keeps its fundamental while the second rank supplies the overblown character.

programs.name: Tuba
programs.description: A single dry 16' rank combines a dark saw with a round sine foundation. A gentle tongue-like onset, stable pitch and short breath release suit low, separated phrases.

programs.name: Brass Octaves
programs.description: Tight 8' and 4' brass ranks with no programmed detune. Matched sustained articulation keeps the octave present throughout the note, with the upper filter opened for its register.

programs.name: Swell And Fall
programs.description: A warm swell becomes dark immediately after note-off, while the amplitude takes longer to disappear. The faster filter release makes the falling color audible inside the tail.

programs.name: Reed Brass
programs.description: A narrow pulse carries a reedy upper edge above a warmer saw body. Distinct filter shapes and a small pressure vibrato make single-line phrases more vocal.

programs.name: Brass Glide Lead
programs.description: A focused brass lead with a small upward scoop, smooth portamento and restrained pressure vibrato. Its softer second rank reinforces the line without becoming a wide section.

programs.name: Tremolo Brass
programs.description: A soft brass pad pulses through the original CHORUS/TREMOLO section. The slower second-rank entrance and sustained body keep the tremolo rounded rather than percussive.

programs.name: Contour Brass
programs.description: A broad keyboard brass voice: a modest treble-brilliance contour and low-register level lift help wide voicings retain their shape. The upper rank stays lighter than the root.

programs.name: Ring Breath Brass
programs.description: A slow, shallow ring-modulator beat adds breathing motion underneath a soft brass chord. The warmer body and slower upper-rank entrance keep the sound smooth.

programs.name: Ensemble Strings
programs.description: A bowed saw body arrives before a quieter PWM section. Gentle chorus joins the ranks; pressure adds bow weight and a restrained vibrato.

programs.name: Slow Strings
programs.description: The body rises over 0.85 seconds and the upper section follows over 1.15 seconds. Hold chords through the opening; the two releases overlap softly.

programs.name: Violins
programs.description: An 8' bowed section with a quieter 4' upper sheen. A quick bow onset and restrained chorus keep articulated lines clear.

programs.name: Cellos
programs.description: A full 16' bowed body with a lighter 8' bow edge. The low filter preserves weight while pressure opens the upper harmonics.

programs.name: Octave Strings
programs.description: Balanced 8' and 4' sections, with the octave entering a little later. Their separate filter ranges keep the upper section present without hollowing the body.

programs.name: PWM Strings
programs.description: Two pulse sections breathe at different slow PWM rates. Moderate pulse motion and a light chorus give shimmer while keeping the pitch centre steady.

programs.name: Thin Strings
programs.description: High-passed saw sections leave a narrow, distant upper-string texture. The second rank is thinner and slower, with little pressure-driven thinning.

programs.name: Dark Strings
programs.description: Covered saw body and soft pulse overtones, with the low end retained. A slow, shallow filter opening gives a sombre held texture.

programs.name: Tremolo Strings
programs.description: A 6.5 Hz square SUB alternates the bow level without silencing the sustain. Quick attacks and light chorus retain the repeated-stroke texture.

programs.name: Solo Violin
programs.description: A single dry 8' saw rank with a small bow-noise component. Velocity shapes the onset; pressure introduces about 16 cents of vibrato. The wheel provides a separate gentle vibrato gesture.

programs.name: Solo Cello
programs.description: A single dry 16' bowed rank with a warm fundamental and a slower bow onset. Pressure adds weight and about 12 cents of vibrato; no octave layer or ensemble chorus is present.

programs.name: Pizzicato Strings
programs.description: A short upper pluck sits above an 8' resonant body. Both ranks decay to silence while the key is held; velocity controls the pluck strength and brightness.

programs.name: Swell Strings
programs.description: A quiet bowed bed gains level and harmonic weight under pressure. Release pressure to return to the soft sustained texture without retriggering the bow.

programs.name: Chamber Strings
programs.description: Two closely tuned bow sections with no chorus. Their modest pulse motion and slightly different attacks suggest a smaller group and preserve clear note changes.

programs.name: Wide Strings
programs.description: Broad stereo sections with slower upper-rank motion and a deeper chorus. The detune stays moderate so sustained chords retain a clear pitch centre.

programs.name: Crystal Strings
programs.description: An 8' bowed body supports a quiet 2' pulse-and-sine sheen. The upper rank opens later and has its own high cutoff for a delicate glassy edge.

programs.name: Fifth Strings
programs.description: A softly entering 5 1/3' upper section adds an open fifth above the 8' body. Play sparse voicings to hear the harmonic interval clearly.

programs.name: Analog Orchestra
programs.description: A warm 16' body and lighter 4' upper section span two octaves. Separate filter ranges and gently staggered bows keep the low section from becoming thin.

programs.name: Spiccato Strings
programs.description: Short rebounding bow strokes: a quick body and an even shorter upper bite, both returning to silence on a held key. Play detached notes for repeated strokes.

programs.name: Bowed Swell Strings
programs.description: The bow level rises first, then the two filters bloom over 1.1 and 1.5 seconds. Hold the chord to let the brighter section emerge from the covered body.

programs.name: Synth Strings Saw
programs.description: Two saw sections with a covered upper spectrum and pronounced chorus. Their shallow filter motion and long overlapping releases make a classic sustained synth-string texture.

programs.name: String Machine
programs.description: Bright saw sections with a fast ensemble chorus, nearly steady sustain and little touch dependence. Short attacks keep chord changes immediate.

programs.name: Contour Strings
programs.description: The keyboard contour softens the bass and adds upper-register brilliance with a small level reduction. A low-pass body and brighter second rank remain balanced across the keyboard.

programs.name: Ring Strings
programs.description: A quiet 0.8 Hz ring component adds a slow level shimmer behind the sustained ensemble. It stays subtle enough for held chords and does not impose a metallic pitch.

programs.name: Velvet Strings
programs.description: Soft saw body, low pulse overtones and a very light chorus. The two long releases make a smooth tail without adding a bright upper layer.

programs.name: Tutti Strings
programs.description: A strong 16' saw body supports an 8' PWM section. Faster bows and a moderate chorus give full, articulated ensemble chords with velocity-dependent attack weight.

programs.name: Marcato Strings
programs.description: An accented upper bow burst settles into a sustained body. Velocity controls both the bite and its weight; the quieter sustained section remains after the accent.

programs.name: Air Strings
programs.description: Quiet filtered bow air fades after the onset behind a sustained saw body. The separate noise envelope leaves only a soft breath during the hold; pressure supports the body.

programs.name: Slow Pad
programs.description: A warm saw body fades in before a brighter moving pulse rank. Their filter blooms and release lengths overlap gently; pressure brings forward the upper color.

programs.name: Ring Drift Pad
programs.description: A steady low-mid body and lighter pulse halo move through a slow ring beat. The ring frequency envelope adds a gentle drift while the held pitch remains recognizable.

programs.name: Choir Pad
programs.description: Two softly entered pulse ranks suggest an open vowel. A low body band supports a brighter nasal band; this is a synthesized choir color.

programs.name: Dark Choir
programs.description: A covered 16' vowel-like body sits beneath a quiet 8' nasal band. Unequal rank attacks give this low choir color depth without a large detuned wobble.

programs.name: Sweep Pad
programs.description: A sustained body opens over three seconds, followed by a higher pulse bloom. Hold beyond four seconds to hear both filter crests and their gradual settling.

programs.name: Breathing Pad
programs.description: A rounded pad gently swells and recedes at 0.7 Hz. The original SUB moves level by a few decibels while slower PWM keeps the upper rank alive.

programs.name: Glass Pad
programs.description: An 8' soft body supports a late 2' sine and pulse glint. The high rank has its own brighter filter and lower sustain, letting the glass color float above the chord.

programs.name: Warm Pad
programs.description: A filtered saw with a small sine foundation and a quiet soft-pulse companion. Compact stereo motion and modest pressure brightness preserve the warm center.

programs.name: Wide Pad
programs.description: Saw and pulse ranks spread left and right with a broad chorus. Their different attacks and PWM rates create width while each side retains a useful chord body.

programs.name: Octave Pad
programs.description: A 16' foundation and an 8' upper rank form one true octave. The lighter upper voice arrives later and fades sooner, leaving a rounded low tail.

programs.name: Fifth Pad
programs.description: An 8' root and a quieter 5 1/3' harmonic fifth bloom together. A restrained upper filter crest and little detune keep the open interval clear.

programs.name: Evolving Pad
programs.description: Different rank envelopes evolve into a softly repeating rising filter motion. The 0.7 Hz original SUB supplies the repeating tilt; slow PWM adds an independent movement.

programs.name: Noise Pad
programs.description: A warm pitched saw sustains beneath a separately enveloped band of air. Pressure emphasizes the noise layer; its longer attack and release frame the airy texture.

programs.name: Pressure Pad
programs.description: A soft, dark bed gains most of its level and upper glow from pressure. The body stays warm as the later pulse rank opens; easing pressure lets the chord recede.

programs.name: Sine Pad
programs.description: Pure 8' and quieter 4' sines fade in at different speeds. Pressure shapes their level, not their bypassed filters; no chorus or added hiss clouds the rounded octave.

programs.name: Hollow Pad
programs.description: Near-square pulses emphasize a hollow odd-harmonic center. Shallow, slow width motion and differently filtered ranks soften the sound without making a thin nasal pulse.

programs.name: Resonant Pad
programs.description: A resonant pulse crest opens above a smoother saw body. The upper filter peaks later and decays faster, giving a moving color without both ranks whistling together.

programs.name: Pulse Pad
programs.description: Two pulse-only ranks use distinct PWM rates and depths. A steady low body anchors the moving upper harmonics, with modest chorus instead of excessive pitch detune.

programs.name: Tremolo Pad
programs.description: A warm body and brighter pulse rank pass through the original tremolo section. The roughly 3.8 Hz level motion stays rounded rather than chopping the chord to silence.

programs.name: Neo-Noir Pad
programs.description: A dark saw foundation supports a later pulse glow, broad chorus and a faint slow ring beat. Long, unequal releases leave a warm cinematic tail after the upper color recedes.

programs.name: Rain Pad
programs.description: An 8 Hz modern sample-and-hold LFO flickers the filters over a soft pulse body and a little band-limited air. The stepped filter motion is inactive in Pure CS-80.

programs.name: Cathedral Pad
programs.description: A slow 16' saw foundation carries a quieter 4' sine two octaves above. The clean upper stop enters later; a long dry release suggests space without hidden reverb.

programs.name: Shimmer Pad
programs.description: A soft 8' chord supports a light 2' pulse shimmer. The high rank is deliberately opened for its register and enters late, separating the upper sparkle from the body.

programs.name: Low Drone
programs.description: Stable 16' ranks sustain a deep drone: a rounded saw foundation and a quieter hollow pulse. Slow entry and a long low tail support held bass notes without constant pitch wobble.

programs.name: Ether Pad
programs.description: A pure 8' sine fades in beneath a separate thin veil of filtered noise. The air arrives later and follows pressure more strongly, leaving the pitched center clean and soft.

programs.name: Velvet Pad
programs.description: Softly filtered saw ranks overlap with shallow, unequal blooms. Modest detune and chorus make a dense, smooth chord; the second rank closes earlier on release.

programs.name: Analog Haze
programs.description: A broad saw and moving pulse cloud with deliberately stronger voice variation. Moderate drift and staggered envelopes give a haze while retaining a recognizable chord center.

programs.name: Bowed Glass
programs.description: Slowly entered 8' and 4' sines pass through light fixed-frequency ring modulation. Inharmonic sidebands form a bowed-glass color; pressure grows the tone through its amplitude.

programs.name: Night Pad
programs.description: A dark low-mid saw body appears before a dim pulse halo. Shallow filter movement, a quiet upper layer and long releases keep the sustained chord spacious and subdued.

programs.name: Arctic Pad
programs.description: A thin, bright 8' saw band supports a quiet 4' pulse sheen. Distinct high-pass bands and later upper entry create an icy texture; moderate chorus supplies width.

programs.name: Poly Stab
programs.description: A dry chord hit with a rounded saw body and shorter bright accent. Both ranks decay away under a held key; velocity controls the bite and level.

programs.name: Poly Brass Stab
programs.description: A brief brass-like opening crest relaxes into a short chord body. The ranks speak at slightly different times and decay fully, giving a compact accented stab.

programs.name: PWM Poly
programs.description: Pulse ranks with separate width rates form a round sustained body and brighter moving edge. The initial accent settles into an animated held chord.

programs.name: Resonant Poly
programs.description: A sharp resonant upper accent sits over a warmer chord body. Unequal filter decay times distinguish the opening bite from the softer held sound.

programs.name: Detuned Poly
programs.description: Full saw ranks beat against each other by 17 cents. The second enters slightly later with a lighter sustain; no chorus masks the direct detuned character.

programs.name: Poly Sweep
programs.description: A quickly established chord opens through staggered filter crests over roughly half a second. Pressure gently brightens the sustain after the opening sweep settles.

programs.name: Velocity Poly
programs.description: Soft strikes stay dark and quiet; hard strikes add substantial level and a bright upper accent. Low static VCA levels make velocity the main dynamic control.

programs.name: Poly Pluck
programs.description: A short bright pulse attack releases into a longer resonant saw body. Both ranks have zero sustain, so held chords decay naturally instead of becoming a pad.

programs.name: Octave Poly
programs.description: A full 8' saw chord carries a lighter 4' crown. The upper filter is opened for its register, and its shorter accent settles without overwhelming the sustained root.

programs.name: Fifth Poly
programs.description: The 8' body and quieter 5 1/3' harmonic fifth form an open chord color. Stable tuning and a lighter sustained upper rank keep the root clear during held voicings.

programs.name: Bright Poly
programs.description: An open saw body and narrow-pulse edge deliver bright, immediate chords. A brief upper accent adds definition while restrained resonance keeps the held sound clear.

programs.name: Dark Poly
programs.description: A filtered saw with a small sine foundation holds the chord beneath a quiet dark pulse. The upper rank closes sooner, leaving a rounded, gently extended release.

programs.name: Hollow Poly
programs.description: Near-square pulses give a hollow, woody chord center. A quieter, slightly narrower upper rank adds a reedy edge; shallow width movement avoids a thin constant sweep.

programs.name: Wide Poly
programs.description: A solid saw and brighter PWM rank spread across the stereo field. Different accent lengths and a broad chorus give width while the sustained chord remains balanced.

programs.name: Poly Swell
programs.description: A soft initial chord grows under pressure. Low static levels leave room for a substantial dynamic swell, and the brighter second rank responds more strongly than the body.

programs.name: Saw Pulse Poly
programs.description: A sustained saw body pairs with a narrower pulse accent. Their distinct spectral and envelope roles remain audible through the short, lightly chorused release.

programs.name: Synthwave Chords
programs.description: Detuned saw chords have a bright opening accent and broad chorus. The second rank sustains more softly and releases sooner, preserving a warm center in the longer retro tail.

programs.name: Square Poly
programs.description: Unmodulated 50-percent pulses give a clear square-wave chord. The upper rank has a shorter accent and brighter filter; light detune adds body without a PWM sweep.

programs.name: Sine Poly
programs.description: A dominant pure sine body is joined by a small filtered saw attack. The harmonic rank decays to a quiet sustain, leaving rounded chords with meaningful velocity response.

programs.name: Contour Poly
programs.description: A rounded bass-register body opens into clearer upper chords through keyboard brilliance contours. A gentle upper level lift supports melody notes without excessive brightness.

programs.name: Ring Poly
programs.description: A soft saw body and sine-supported pulse edge acquire modest metallic sidebands from the ring modulator. The dry sound retains its pitch and short chord articulation.

programs.name: Glide Poly
programs.description: Sustained saw and pulse chords use gentle polyphonic portamento. Softer onsets let pitch slides speak, while matched rank releases keep the arriving harmony coherent.

programs.name: Tremolo Poly
programs.description: A sustained saw body and softer square rank pass through moderate 5.4 Hz tremolo. The opening accent settles quickly so the held chord's rhythmic level motion stays clear.

programs.name: Poly Sub Pulse
programs.description: A 4 Hz square SUB switches between two filter colors on a sustained chord. The lower saw stays present while the resonant pulse emphasizes the rhythmic brightness change.

programs.name: Electric Piano I
programs.description: A rounded 8' resonator rings beneath a separately decaying strike. Soft touches stay mellow; firm strikes bring forward the short upper bark. Release the key to damp the body.

programs.name: Electric Piano II
programs.description: A warm 8' body supports a shorter 4' tine-like edge. Light chorus widens the decay without obscuring the strike; velocity moves the sound from round to bright.

programs.name: Tine Piano
programs.description: A long rounded body and a shorter third-harmonic strike, with a faint fixed-frequency ring edge. Firm strikes emphasize the metallic attack; the body continues after the upper rank fades.

programs.name: Clavichord I
programs.description: A dry narrow-pulse string body with a short tangent-like upper attack. The two ranks decay independently, and harder strikes add both level and bite.

programs.name: Clavichord II
programs.description: A darker, nasal clavichord interpretation with a resonant opening bite and a dry string decay. The narrow upper rank supplies the short attack rather than a held pad.

programs.name: Funky Clavichord
programs.description: A strong resonant snap over a compact string body. Velocity opens the attack dramatically, while the low high-pass setting preserves the note's weight.

programs.name: Harpsichord I
programs.description: A bright 8' plucked register with a short quill-like edge and a longer string body. Nearly even strike level and quick key-off damping give it a deliberate harpsichord response.

programs.name: Harpsichord II
programs.description: Coupled 8' and 4' plucked registers: the octave is bright at the strike and decays sooner than the lower strings. Little velocity variation keeps the double-register character even.

programs.name: Lute Harpsichord
programs.description: A muted buff-stop interpretation: dark plucked strings with a restrained, quickly vanishing quill edge. The body decays naturally and damps promptly on release.

programs.name: Toy Piano
programs.description: A small high-register metal-bar interpretation: a 2' resonator under a short narrow-pulse strike, with a modest inharmonic ring edge. The attack is much shorter than the ringing body.

programs.name: Honky Keys
programs.description: Two independently decaying 8' string ranks give a deliberately detuned upright-like beating. A strong strike brightens the attack, then both ranks settle into a rounded decay.

programs.name: Vibes Keys
programs.description: A long 8' sine body with a shorter octave strike. Gentle 5 Hz amplitude motion shades the ringing decay; release damps it. Velocity makes the upper attack more apparent.

programs.name: Celesta
programs.description: A delicate 4' bell-like body with a brief 2' attack partial. The upper rank disappears first, leaving a clean high-register decay with no held sustain.

programs.name: Saw Pulse Piano
programs.description: A clearly synthetic piano: a saw body decays beneath a quicker pulse hammer. Firm strikes produce a broad bright attack; the two filters close at different rates.

programs.name: Soft Keys
programs.description: A soft rounded resonator with a subdued felt-like strike. A slightly cushioned onset and restrained upper rank suit quiet chords; harder playing still has usable dynamic range.

programs.name: Chorus Keys
programs.description: Bright electric keys with a clear transient and a lightly chorused resonant body. The upper strike decays quickly enough to keep chord changes distinct.

programs.name: Stage Keys
programs.description: A forward piano-like attack over a long, rounded resonator. The bright rank fades first, giving sustained chords room without leaving a static organ-like tail.

programs.name: Velocity Keys
programs.description: Wide touch dynamics: soft strikes reveal the round body, while hard strikes strongly raise the bright attack rank. Both layers decay, so held keys do not leave a fixed sustaining tone.

programs.name: Dulcimer
programs.description: Hammered-string interpretation with an 8' body and a shorter bright 4' strike. The opening clang settles into a clean ringing decay; harder strikes bring out the upper course.

programs.name: Reed Piano
programs.description: A pulse-rich reed body with a separate short bark. Hard strikes open the resonant upper edge; the warm lower body decays more slowly and damps on key release.

programs.name: Glass Keys
programs.description: A clear 4' sine resonator with a shorter 2' glint. Shallow chorus gives the decay a glassy movement; both ranks fade completely under held keys.

programs.name: Tremolo Keys
programs.description: A rounded electric-key body with a crisp upper strike, shaded by moderate tremolo. The ringing body carries the motion after the short attack rank has faded.

programs.name: Contour Keys
programs.description: Electric keys balanced across the keyboard: a fuller low body and more present treble attack. The contour adds register contrast while the strike and body retain separate decays.

programs.name: Pressure Keys
programs.description: A percussive piano-like strike settles into a quiet held body. Press into that remaining body to raise and brighten it; the short hammer rank stays percussive.

programs.name: Flute Organ 8+4
programs.description: An 8' sine body with a quieter 4' flute stop. Straight tuning, a fast soft gate and steady, velocity-independent sustain keep chord voicings clear.

programs.name: Flute Organ 16+8
programs.description: A full 16' flute body supported by an 8' sine stop. The lower rank speaks slightly more slowly; both remain steady while held.

programs.name: Percussive Organ
programs.description: An 8' sustained sine body with true second-harmonic percussion at 4'. The separate percussion rank decays while the fundamental remains held; play separated notes to retrigger it.

programs.name: Reed Organ
programs.description: Two stable 8' pulse ranks combine a hollow square body with a smaller, brighter reed band. A short bellows-like onset and release soften the steady registration.

programs.name: Church Organ
programs.description: A rounded 16' saw principal with a restrained 4' sine stop. The two pipe-like onsets differ slightly; the dry release leaves room for the host's room or hall reverb.

programs.name: Chapel Organ
programs.description: A soft 8' flute with a small 2' stop adding a clear upper edge. Gentle pipe speech and a compact release suit exposed, quiet chords.

programs.name: Theatre Organ
programs.description: Warm 8' and 4' ranks combine flute body and restrained reed harmonics. Moderate tremulant movement and a slight rank offset animate sustained theatre-style chords.

programs.name: Tremolo Organ
programs.description: A weighty 16' sine with a quieter 4' flute stop, moving under a relaxed tremolo. Stable pitches and restrained depth keep the bass line intelligible.

programs.name: Mellow Organ
programs.description: One 8' sine rank with a soft gate and no upper registration. Straight pitch, no chorus and a short release give a clean, rounded accompaniment.

programs.name: Bright Organ
programs.description: An open 8' saw principal is supported by a small 2' sine stop. Brightness comes from harmonic registration, with a crisp gate and steady level across key velocities.

programs.name: Pipe Organ
programs.description: A stopped 16' pulse foundation and a clearer 4' saw principal form a full pipe registration. Separate onset and release times preserve the two stops without ensemble detuning.

programs.name: Combo Organ
programs.description: A nasal 8' pulse body and a quieter 4' pulse stop, with a restrained chorus. Fast keying keeps rhythmic comping defined while the two pulse widths distinguish the registration.

programs.name: Fifth Organ
programs.description: An 8' sine and a quieter 5 1/3' quint stop in the harmonic 3:2 ratio. The upper stop stays subordinate, with straight tuning and sustained organ keying.

programs.name: Organ Vibrato
programs.description: An 8'+4' flute registration with gentle 6.2 Hz SUB vibrato. The roughly eight-cent pitch motion adds movement without turning held chords into a broad wobble.

programs.name: Flute
programs.description: Rounded 8' body with quiet upper harmonics and a separate sustained air rank. Velocity shapes the attack; pressure adds breath and gentle vibrato.

programs.name: Breathy Flute
programs.description: Soft pitched body with a separately sustained, band-limited air stream. Pressure increases the breath as well as the body; use a gentle attack.

programs.name: Pan Flute
programs.description: A short, independent noise chiff precedes the sustained 8' body. The air rank decays to silence while the held pitch remains; velocity controls the tongued onset.

programs.name: Recorder
programs.description: An 8' sine reinforced by quiet odd harmonics, with a brief tongue transient. Clear, nearly straight tone and a quick release suit articulated lines.

programs.name: Clarinet
programs.description: A centered 8' square supplies the hollow odd-harmonic body. A short tongue and restrained breath rank support the onset; pressure opens the reed without a broad pitch wobble.

programs.name: Bass Clarinet
programs.description: Both ranks follow the same 16' fundamental: a hollow square body and a quiet upper reed band. Slow breath onset and restrained pressure vibrato keep the low register clear.

programs.name: Oboe
programs.description: A narrow 8' pulse gives the focused double-reed body; a quieter saw rank adds a nasal upper band. Distinct rank attacks soften the tongue while pressure adds controlled intensity.

programs.name: English Horn
programs.description: A darker double-reed interpretation for the lower middle register. The rounded fundamental and quieter nasal rank share 8' tuning, with a broader breath onset than Oboe.

programs.name: Bassoon
programs.description: Two 16' reed ranks combine a woody low body with a smaller, nasal overtone band. Shorter release and a definite tongue keep low-register phrases articulate.

programs.name: Soprano Reed
programs.description: A bright 8' saw body and narrow-pulse reed band for upper-register lines. Pressure adds brightness and a small vibrato; a subtle upward onset scoop keeps hard attacks expressive.

programs.name: Ocarina
programs.description: A soft 4' vessel-flute sine with a trace of separately filtered air. No lower pitched rank is mixed in; pressure changes level and adds restrained vibrato.

programs.name: Piccolo
programs.description: An agile 2' body with a small filtered harmonic component and a short air onset. Both ranks are registered at 2'; there is no unintended lower-octave sine.

programs.name: Whistle
programs.description: One clear 4' sine rises gently into pitch with a short glide. The second rank is silent in the mix; velocity and pressure shape level, with optional gentle vibrato.

programs.name: Shakuhachi
programs.description: A rounded 8' body follows an aspirated noise attack that settles to quiet breath. Initial bend rises into the note; pressure adds controlled vibrato and breath intensity.

programs.name: Guitar I
programs.description: A warm 8' string body beneath a short, brighter pick rank. Harder strikes increase the pick as well as the body; the upper edge fades first, leaving a dry natural-style decay.

programs.name: Guitar II
programs.description: A brighter, longer-ringing guitar interpretation with a firm pick and a clear string center. The two ranks have independent decays, so the attack does not remain as a sustained buzz.

programs.name: Funky Pluck I
programs.description: A compact resonant snap over a rounded pulse body. The opening edge closes quickly and both ranks decay fully, making repeated short notes articulate cleanly.

programs.name: Funky Pluck II
programs.description: A broader wah-shaped pluck: the body filter closes more slowly while a short upper snap marks the strike. Hold for the rounded decay or release early for a damped phrase.

programs.name: Harp
programs.description: A long 8' resonant body with a shorter 4' finger-plucked glint. The upper harmonics fade first, leaving a round clear tail; release controls the damping.

programs.name: Koto
programs.description: A focused narrow-pulse string with a sharp plectrum edge and a slight upward settling of the initial pitch. The pick rank dies quickly while the string body rings.

programs.name: Banjo
programs.description: A short nasal string body with a very brief noisy pick edge. The high harmonics fall away quickly, giving a dry banjo-like articulation suited to repeated notes.

programs.name: Mandolin
programs.description: Two close 8' string courses with independent decays and a small 12 Hz level flutter. Play repeated notes for tremolo picking; the paired ranks keep the attacks bright and compact.

programs.name: Drone Pluck
programs.description: A resonant picked onset settles into a quiet held drone with a faint metallic ring. Pressure raises the remaining body after the short pick rank has disappeared.

programs.name: Nylon Pluck
programs.description: A rounded sine-and-saw body with a separate soft finger transient. Its short, mellow edge and trace of air disappear rapidly; the warm string center rings without chorus or detuning.

programs.name: Steel Pluck
programs.description: Paired 8' and 4' steel-string courses with a bright opening shimmer. The octave course fades faster than the body, and a very small tuning offset adds restrained beating.

programs.name: Muted Pluck
programs.description: A palm-muted pulse body with a brief pick click. Both ranks die quickly even while the note is held; the low body retains weight beneath the short upper attack.

programs.name: Kalimba
programs.description: A clear 4' tine-like body with a brief 2' strike harmonic. The upper ping falls away early, leaving a stable round decay; velocity determines how prominently it speaks.

programs.name: Zither
programs.description: Bright paired 8' strings with a long body decay and an independently fading upper course. Shallow chorus and a small tuning offset supply a restrained ensemble shimmer.

programs.name: Dulcimer Pluck
programs.description: An articulate 8' saw body with a bright, short 4' pulse pick. The octave edge decays much sooner than the lower string, giving a clear plucked-course attack.

programs.name: Pressure Pluck
programs.description: A short picked edge over a decaying body that leaves a quiet held bed. Press into the remaining body to swell and brighten it after the pick; release the key to damp it.

programs.name: Analog Bass
programs.description: A stable 16' saw-and-sine foundation with a shorter 8' pulse attack. Velocity adds bite and level; the dry body remains clear under held notes.

programs.name: Resonance Bass
programs.description: A resonant upper attack sweeps into a firm low body. A small sine foundation preserves weight while the filter peak provides the character.

programs.name: Sine Bass
programs.description: A sustained 16' sine with a separate, very short 8' pulse click. The upper rank disappears after the onset, leaving a clean low fundamental.

programs.name: Sub Bass
programs.description: One centered 16' sine, with a short rounded onset and controlled release. Velocity controls level; there is no detuned upper layer, filter sweep or vibrato.

programs.name: Pluck Bass
programs.description: A resonant low pluck with a separately decaying upper attack. Both ranks fall to silence on a held key; the body outlasts the bright initial edge.

programs.name: Fretless Glide
programs.description: A soft fingered attack and a long, gently decaying 16' body. Short portamento joins phrases; pressure adds a small pitch vibrato and a warmer singing edge.

programs.name: Funk Bass
programs.description: A tight, velocity-sensitive filter pluck over a rounded low body. Harder strikes emphasize the upper snap; both ranks decay for clearly separated rhythmic notes.

programs.name: Brass Bass
programs.description: A 16' saw body grows into an 8' brass edge, with a compact filter bloom. Pressure opens the held sound without washing out the low foundation.

programs.name: Octave Bass
programs.description: Stable 16' and 8' saws with separate low-body and upper-octave envelopes. The octave remains present in the sustain, rather than becoming only a click.

programs.name: Pulse Bass
programs.description: Two 16' pulses with restrained, differently paced PWM. A small sine foundation keeps the low end steady as the harmonic width moves.

programs.name: Round Bass
programs.description: A smooth 16' sine-and-soft-saw body, with a quiet same-register harmonic edge. Little resonance and a rounded onset suit warm, even bass lines.

programs.name: Velocity Bass
programs.description: Soft strikes give a rounded low body; hard strikes bring forward a brighter upper attack and much stronger level. Pressure does not override the struck dynamic.

programs.name: Rubber Bass
programs.description: A small upward pitch scoop rises into each note, followed by a rounded resonant pluck. The short upper attack makes the springy onset clear without an ongoing pitch wobble.

programs.name: Dark Bass
programs.description: A deep 16' foundation with a deliberately dark, same-register saw shadow. The bypass sine preserves the fundamental while the filtered harmonics stay restrained.

programs.name: Bright Bass
programs.description: A full 16' body with a cutting 8' saw edge. The upper rank settles after the attack, keeping the held bass bright without overwhelming its foundation.

programs.name: Picked Bass
programs.description: A short pulse-and-noise pick transient sits above a longer decaying 16' string body. Hard strikes sharpen the pick; the upper rank does not persist through the held note.

programs.name: Upright Pluck
programs.description: A rounded decaying 16' body with a separate woody finger-and-string transient. This synthesized upright interpretation favors lower notes and short, connected phrases.

programs.name: Fifth Bass
programs.description: A 16' foundation supports a quieter 5 1/3' upper twelfth: the fifth above its octave. The upper harmonic has a shorter attack accent and a controlled sustain.

programs.name: Pedal Bass
programs.description: Steady 16' and quieter 8' sine stops, with rounded keying and a short release. Like an organ pedal registration, its level is independent of strike velocity.

programs.name: Squelch Bass
programs.description: A quick, strongly resonant upper sweep over a compact low body. Velocity opens the squelch; the low sine component prevents the resonance from hollowing out the bass.

programs.name: Ring Bass
programs.description: A stable low body and narrower upper pulse feed a light 35 Hz ring blend. The audible low-rate sidebands add a rough growl while the dry component keeps the note centered.

programs.name: Sub Wobble Bass
programs.description: A 3 Hz SUB sine moves the filtered harmonic layer while a bypass sine keeps the low foundation steady. Hold notes for the rhythmic filter motion; there is no pitch wobble.

programs.name: Pressure Bass
programs.description: A playable low body is present at the strike. Pressure brings forward a brighter upper rank and opens the filters while the sine-supported fundamental stays firm.

programs.name: Contour Bass
programs.description: A dry saw-and-pulse bass whose low-key level contour restrains boom. Upper notes gain a little brightness, keeping runs clearer across the keyboard.

programs.name: Touch Lead
programs.description: A firm saw body with a lighter pulse edge. Velocity shapes the onset; pressure adds level, brilliance and gentle vibrato. The wheel supplies additional controlled vibrato.

programs.name: Aftertouch Vibrato Lead
programs.description: A centered, singing lead whose vibrato grows with pressure to roughly a quarter-tone peak-to-peak. The dry tone remains stable until pressure or wheel is applied.

programs.name: Ribbon Glide Lead
programs.description: A smooth, centered lead for ribbon gestures. Short portamento and a small upward onset scoop connect phrases; a restrained upper edge keeps large slides readable.

programs.name: Noir Lead
programs.description: A dark saw body blooms into a later brass edge. Pressure opens the sustained tone and adds controlled vibrato; moderate chorus and a long release support spacious single lines.

programs.name: Neo-Noir Brass Lead
programs.description: A broader, darker brass lead with a slower upper-rank bloom and a sustained release. Pressure brings out the brighter crown while moderate detune supplies width.

programs.name: Glide Lead
programs.description: A steady saw-and-pulse tone with long, smooth portamento between notes. Gentle envelope motion keeps the glide audible without adding an onset pitch scoop.

programs.name: Sine Lead
programs.description: One pure 8' sine with a rounded onset. Pressure controls level and a gentle vibrato; filter brilliance is intentionally inactive on this bypass-sine voice.

programs.name: Whistle Lead
programs.description: A single 4' sine with a small upward scoop and quick breath-like articulation. Pressure adds restrained vibrato and level; no lower-octave rank is mixed in.

programs.name: Square Lead
programs.description: A hollow 8' square body with a quieter same-register square edge. Nearly unison tuning and dry, quick articulation preserve the centered odd-harmonic character.

programs.name: Narrow Pulse Lead
programs.description: A narrow pulse body with a lighter, differently voiced pulse edge. The dry, nasal tone has a clear attack and restrained vibrato for agile lines.

programs.name: Resonant Lead
programs.description: A moving resonant edge above a warmer body. Pressure raises the filter focus while modest low-cut settings retain a pitched foundation.

programs.name: Screaming Lead
programs.description: A focused, aggressive upper resonance responds strongly to pressure. A quieter saw-and-sine body holds the pitch beneath the brighter edge; vibrato stays controlled.

programs.name: Fifth Lead
programs.description: An 8' body with a lighter 5 1/3' rank at a harmonic fifth. The upper voice has its own brighter filter and slower onset, preserving clarity in the interval.

programs.name: Octave Lead
programs.description: A solid 8' saw under a sustained 4' pulse crown. The octave has a higher cutoff and a lighter level, so its presence stays clear without taking over the lead.

programs.name: Soft Lead
programs.description: A rounded saw-and-sine body with a quiet soft pulse edge. Gently staggered attacks and restrained pressure brightness keep slow phrases warm and centered.

programs.name: Init Bend Lead
programs.description: A clear upward scoop begins below each struck note and settles quickly into a bright sustained lead. Harder strikes deepen the scoop; there is no constant pitch modulation.

programs.name: Pressure Lead
programs.description: Requires poly or channel aftertouch: hold a key and press to bring the sound out of silence. On screen, drag down on a held key. Pressure controls level and brightness; releasing pressure fades the tone.

programs.name: Velocity Lead
programs.description: Strike velocity controls a wide range of level and brightness. The quiet static gain lets soft notes stay soft, while hard strikes reveal a more prominent pulse edge.

programs.name: Detuned Lead
programs.description: Two sustained saw ranks with a deliberate 12-cent offset. Their different filters and attacks create a broad beating lead without added chorus or deep pressure vibrato.

programs.name: Sub Vibrato Lead
programs.description: A smooth lead with a continuous, restrained 5.2 Hz vibrato. Pressure adds a small amount of depth and level, allowing the held tone to sing without a wide pitch wobble.

programs.name: Trill Lead
programs.description: A square SUB alternates approximately one semitone below and above the played pitch at 6 Hz. Pressure and wheel pitch routes are disabled so the interval remains deliberate.

programs.name: Glissando Lead
programs.description: A clearly articulated lead whose portamento steps through semitones. The steady sustain and simple filter motion keep the discrete glissando easy to hear.

programs.name: Brass Lead
programs.description: A compact brass rise for single lines: the warm body arrives before the brighter saw edge. Pressure adds a controlled bloom; the release stays short enough for clear phrasing.

programs.name: Reed Lead
programs.description: A focused pulse body and a quieter nasal edge form a dry reed-like lead. Modest pressure brilliance and vibrato shape phrases without removing the fundamental.

programs.name: Wah Lead
programs.description: Pressure brings a 3.8 Hz SUB sine into the resonant filter route. The unpressed note stays centered; leaning in adds a rhythmic wah without also creating pitch vibrato.

programs.name: Ring Lead
programs.description: A clean center tone mixed with 280 Hz ring sidebands for a metallic edge. The restrained wet blend preserves pitch identity while pressure brightens the source.

programs.name: Hollow Lead
programs.description: A near-square body and a quieter moving pulse create a hollow tone with slow harmonic motion. The lower-width body stays stable while the second rank carries most of the PWM.

programs.name: Ether Lead
programs.description: One 8' sine with a soft onset, long glide and expressive pressure level. Gentle pressure vibrato gives a theremin-like gesture without an unintended beating second oscillator.

programs.name: Solo Synth
programs.description: A bright, agile saw lead with a lightly supporting pulse edge. Quick articulation, useful velocity contrast and modest pressure vibrato suit exposed melodic lines.

programs.name: Contour Lead
programs.description: A rounded lower register opens progressively into brighter upper notes. A gentle high-key level trim balances that added brilliance while retaining clear solo articulation.

programs.name: Ring Bell I
programs.description: A clear 8' sine body rings beneath a brief octave strike. A fixed 307 Hz ring carrier adds inharmonic sidebands; harder playing brings out the impact.

programs.name: Ring Bell II
programs.description: A warmer bell body with a sharp 2 2/3' upper mode. Its lower ring carrier and shorter, brighter impact distinguish it from Ring Bell I.

programs.name: Tubular Bells
programs.description: A long 16' tube body follows a bright, quickly fading upper strike. Moderate ring sidebands add metal while the dry low mode keeps the note grounded.

programs.name: Glockenspiel
programs.description: A bright 4' metal bar sustains after a hard 2' attack. The two decay times preserve a clear struck pitch beneath the high ring shimmer.

programs.name: Celeste Bells
programs.description: A rounded sine body and soft octave hammer suggest a celeste. Light ring color and restrained chorus leave a delicate, stable center to the note.

programs.name: Music Box
programs.description: A small 4' tine keeps a short, pure tail after a tiny 2' pluck. A trace of ring modulation supplies metallic color without obscuring the melody.

programs.name: Gong
programs.description: A deep sine mode blooms under a noisy upper clang. The ring carrier settles after impact, and the shorter metal layer recedes into a long low resonance.

programs.name: Temple Bell
programs.description: A deep 16' bell with a clear upper mode and a slowly settling ring carrier. The upper strike fades early, leaving a calm, long low tail.

programs.name: Marimba
programs.description: An unmodulated sine body is struck by a short, filtered fourth-harmonic pulse. The upper wooden knock dies well before the rounded body; velocity emphasizes the mallet.

programs.name: Vibraphone
programs.description: A long sine bar and shorter octave overtone share smooth 5.2 Hz SUB tremolo. The amplitude motion leaves a continuous ringing body between its crests.

programs.name: Xylophone
programs.description: A bright 4' wooden body follows a very brief 2' knock. No ring or vibrato is added, so fast lines keep a dry, clearly pitched attack.

programs.name: Crystal Bell
programs.description: A high sine body and a brittle upper strike produce a glassy bell. Stronger high-frequency ring sidebands hang over the clean dry mode as the impact fades.

programs.name: Bell Pad
programs.description: A struck upper edge gives way to a quiet sustained bell body. Moderate ring color, restrained chorus and unequal long releases support held chords.

programs.name: Ring Sweep Bell
programs.description: A fast ring-envelope rise sweeps the carrier upward at impact, then it falls back over the resonating sine body. The upper strike is shorter than the moving ring tail.

programs.name: Steel Drum
programs.description: A rounded sine-and-pulse body rings after an octave mallet strike. Mild ring sidebands and a closing body filter suggest a shallow steel pan.

programs.name: Chimes
programs.description: High 4' and 2' modes ring with unequal long decays. A light pulse edge marks the strike, then the pure upper chime and metallic sidebands linger.

programs.name: Dark Bell
programs.description: A low 16' sine hangs under a subdued 8' strike. The short filtered upper edge and low ring carrier keep the attack audible without a bright metallic wash.

programs.name: Bell Choir
programs.description: An 8' bell and a 5 1/3' bell sing a fifth apart. The upper voice decays sooner, with modest chorus and ring color joining the two resonances.

programs.name: Metallic Keys
programs.description: A high-passed saw body is struck by a much shorter, brighter octave saw. Ring sidebands give a metallic edge while a little bypass sine anchors the pitched tail.

programs.name: Agogo
programs.description: A hollow high pulse body and a short upper knock make a compact metal-bell hit. Strong ring color and resonant filtering give the strike a nasal clang.

programs.name: Clock Bells
programs.description: The 4' and 2 2/3' ranks sound a true fifth apart. A small upper impact gives way to two clear, unequal bell decays with restrained ring color.

programs.name: Ring Mallet
programs.description: A rounded 8' body follows a short 2 2/3' mallet strike. Stronger initial-level response on the upper rank makes hard hits brighter and more metallic.

programs.name: Random Filter
programs.description: Modern sample-and-hold steps the resonant filters at 7.5 Hz. A saw body and lighter octave pulse make each held random cutoff audible as a computer-like burble.

programs.name: Random Pitch Blips
programs.description: Modern sample-and-hold picks small, unquantized pitch steps around the played key at 6.5 Hz. A matching square amplitude LFO separates the sine-and-pulse tone into blips.

programs.name: Siren
programs.description: A sine body and quiet octave harmonic follow a smooth three-semitone peak-to-peak SUB wail. Rounded onset and release avoid clicks; pressure quickens the siren.

programs.name: Laser Zap
programs.description: A resonant pulse sweep drops sharply after the strike, with no bypass sine masking the descent. A separate, very short noise flash adds the laser's initial snap.

programs.name: Wind
programs.description: A low noise bed and a separate airy gust band move through a slow SUB filter swell. Pressure brings up the upper air; soft, unequal releases let the gust subside.

programs.name: Surf
programs.description: A slow falling SUB saw shapes repeated crests of bright wash over a continuous low surf bed. Separate noise bands and envelope times give each wave weight and spray.

programs.name: Sci-Fi Drone
programs.description: A dark 16' saw-and-sine foundation supports a later third-harmonic pulse. Slow ring beating and gentle filter drift animate the held drone without a sharp attack.

programs.name: Robot Voice
programs.description: A hollow pulse band and a brighter saw band close after a short consonant-like onset. A 73 Hz ring carrier adds robotic buzz; pressure opens the two bands.

programs.name: Alarm
programs.description: A clear 4' call alternates between two pitches three semitones apart. A quieter low pulse gives the onset weight while square SUB level motion accents the two-tone warning.

programs.name: Space Sweep
programs.description: A low body and later upper pulse bloom as the ring carrier rises, then falls over several seconds. Different filter and amplitude swells make the motion unfold in layers.

programs.name: Bubbles
programs.description: An 11 Hz modern sample-and-hold LFO jumps two resonant filter bands. A soft pulse supplies the hollow bubble body and a little filtered noise adds the popping edge.

programs.name: Thunder
programs.description: A short bright noise crack precedes a much longer low filtered rumble. Slow, shallow SUB motion moves the rolling tail; velocity controls the force of the strike.

programs.name: Rain
programs.description: A continuous midband rain bed sits below finer upper droplets. Modern sample-and-hold changes the noise level at 16 Hz, with the quieter upper band flickering more deeply.

programs.name: Helicopter
programs.description: A low 16' pulse engine and a separate rotor-noise band throb at 11.5 Hz. SUB level and filter pulses leave the underlying engine audible; pressure accelerates the rotor.

programs.name: UFO Landing
programs.description: A low sine body follows repeating downward SUB glides while the ring carrier settles after each note. A shorter upper pulse edge marks the start of the landing sweep.

programs.name: Telemetry
programs.description: A high narrow pulse alternates pitches at 7 Hz, with a sharper 2' onset edge. Brief release and shallow level pulses keep the electronic signal dry and articulated.

programs.name: Clockwork
programs.description: Six-Hz modern amplitude pulses form dry mechanical ticks from a high pulse and thin noise edge. Slower SUB filter steps add a tick-tock change of color.

programs.name: Deep Space
programs.description: A very slow 16' sine bloom carries a later, cloudy noise band. Gentle sub-hertz ring beating and long independent releases leave a deep, moving tail.

programs.name: Metal Scrape
programs.description: A resonant saw-and-noise body follows a short high noise scrape. The ring carrier falls quickly after impact, adding a rough metallic edge to the closing filter bands.

programs.name: Machine Hum
programs.description: A steady 16' pulse motor supports a quieter upper mechanical buzz. A fixed 50 Hz ring carrier supplies sidebands, with a gradual start and a short coast after release.

programs.name: Sweep Riser
programs.description: Hold a note for the five-second resonant rise: a low saw body opens across six filter octaves while a later noise layer blooms above it. The peak then settles gradually.

programs.name: Downer
programs.description: A bright held saw falls into a low filter setting when the key is released. The longer body release keeps that downward sweep audible after the shorter noisy upper edge fades.

programs.name: Glitch Sub
programs.description: Thirty-Hz SUB filter steps roughen a low pulse into a digital-sounding buzz. A shorter upper saw edge marks each keystroke, while shallow level pulses reinforce the flutter.

programs.name: Breath FX
programs.description: A soft low breath band supports a faster upper-air layer. Pressure raises the airy rank more strongly and gently opens both filters, giving a controllable exhale and fade.

programs.name: Delay Brass
programs.description: Play clipped midrange chords; the opening brass swell leaves gaps for 375 ms echoes. Lean into pressure to brighten held notes.

programs.name: Plate Pad
programs.description: Hold open chords around C3-C5; a soft lower pulse blooms beneath an octave sheen. Release between changes to hear the warm plate tail.

programs.name: Phaser Strings
programs.description: Bow connected chords in C3-C5 and hold the ends of phrases. A bright saw section and quieter pulse band expose the phaser's slow moving notches.

programs.name: Drive Lead
programs.description: Play firm lines in C4-C6: a pulse body carries a shorter saw edge into warm drive. Pressure adds bite and restrained vibrato.

programs.name: Arp Poly
programs.description: Hold two to four notes around C3-C4 for eight notes per second across two octaves. A short octave accent and one-second filter cycle articulate the ascent.

programs.name: Arp Bells
programs.description: Hold a small chord around C4 for four notes per second, rising and falling over two octaves. A short third-harmonic strike leaves space for 375 ms echoes.

programs.name: Arp Bass
programs.description: Hold a root and fifth around C3 for a six-note-per-second bass pattern. A compact 16' body and short 8' snap follow a gentle four-step filter cycle.

programs.name: LFO Sweep Pad
programs.description: Hold spacious chords for at least ten seconds. A broad triangle filter sweep moves over a warm low body, with slower irregular stereo drift.

programs.name: LFO Pan Keys
programs.description: Play relaxed C3-C6 chords and let them ring. The rounded body rocks left to right once per second while its brighter octave strike fades first.

programs.name: PWM LFO Strings
programs.description: Sustain midrange chords: two differently biased pulse ranks share a slow triangle width sweep. The later, brighter rank adds a gentle shimmer.

programs.name: Stereo Delay Pluck
programs.description: Play sparse picked figures around C3-C5. A warm pulse string and short octave pick feed 250 ms stereo echoes; lift early for clean gaps.

programs.name: Ambient Bells
programs.description: Strike widely spaced notes around C4-C6 and allow the decay to clear. A rounded fundamental outlasts the upper fifth; quiet 560 ms echoes open into a dark plate.

programs.name: Ensemble Plus
programs.description: Use open midrange voicings and sustain through the staggered onset. Light original chorus and a shallow three-tap ensemble broaden the saw/pulse section.

programs.name: Space Lead
programs.description: Connect single lines in C4-C6 with short slides and leave room for 400 ms echoes. Pressure introduces gentle vibrato; the dry release keeps phrase endings clear.

programs.name: Random Arp
programs.description: Hold a small chord near C3 for six random notes per second over two octaves. Sample-and-hold brightness changes at half the note rate; short releases separate the notes.

programs.name: Drive Bass
programs.description: Play short bass lines around C3. A firm 16' pulse-and-sine body anchors a brief 8' rasp; firmer strikes add level and bite, while parallel drive gently smooths the edge.

programs.name: Phased Polysynth
programs.description: Use compact rhythmic chords in C3-C5. A broad saw body follows a sharper pulse accent; the phaser animates the held tail, with a short plate after release.

programs.name: Tremolo LFO Organ
programs.description: Hold chords around C3-C5 for a steady four-pulse-per-second tremolo. The 8' body has a little reed edge; pressure brings forward the sustained 4' stop.

programs.name: Init Circuit
programs.description: A clean starting point on the circuit engine: one saw rank, open filter, no modulation.
